episode_title: CEO @ Webflow | Preventing Burnout When AI Won’t Slow Down

real_qa.q: How is Webflow transforming its business with AI and agentic marketing capabilities?
real_qa.r: Webflow started as a website builder and evolved into a digital experience platform supporting content publishing, updates, analytics, experimentation, and growth. More recently, the company has transformed into an agentic marketing platform with agents that run on top of the software and deliver value autonomously. This transformation is driven by continuous moments of opportunity as AI capabilities evolve, requiring the company to ask itself what needs to be done to ensure long-term business outcomes and meet customer needs.
real_qa.requete: Webflow agentic marketing platform AI transformation

real_qa.q: Why does Linda Tong believe saying no is the cleanest sign someone is good at their job?
real_qa.r: Someone told her early in her career that to be good at your job—whether as a PM, business person, salesperson, or marketer—the sign that signals you are good is that you say no more than you say yes. The power of saying no comes from having clarity about what to do and where to focus your time, whereas saying yes often comes from a lack of conviction. This is especially critical now because the friction to building anything has disappeared, making it essential to ask whether something is actually worth doing rather than just doing it because you can.
real_qa.requete: Linda Tong saying no leadership decision making

real_qa.q: What are the top hiring criteria Linda Tong prioritizes for Webflow roles in 2026?
real_qa.r: The two most important characteristics are curiosity and resilience. Curiosity—especially a growth mindset with the desire to learn and experiment—is critical because the world is constantly changing. Resilience is now more relevant than ever due to change fatigue and burnout in the industry. Linda emphasizes that resilience is something you build throughout your life, and while it's undervalued, it is so critical in the current environment.

real_qa.q: How does Webflow implement forced time off and builder days to prevent employee burnout?
real_qa.r: Webflow has built in refresh days—started during COVID but now more critical—to give people forced days off to recuperate. The company also implements builder days where employees go heads down to build and experiment. These initiatives address the hard mental model people are balancing: the concept of work versus working on yourself. By intentionally structuring time for productivity, learning, and rest, Webflow tries to give people a system where they can balance strategic work, learning, and the rest their brains need.
real_qa.requete: Webflow refresh days builder days employee burnout prevention

real_qa.q: What is Project Assassin and why did Webflow undertake feature deprecation?
real_qa.r: Project Assassin was an initiative at Linda's previous company to clean up a product that had millions of features jammed into the UI, most of which weren't really used. A whole team went through the product to identify what should be cut—features unused or used minimally, taking up visual real estate and creating testing baggage. This taught the organization that deprecating features is 10 times harder than building them because of existing users, dependencies, and migration timelines, making leaders far more discerning about what they build initially.
real_qa.requete: Project Assassin feature deprecation product cleanup
